extracted.intended_audience: R package authors and volunteer reviewers considering participation in rOpenSci's Software Peer Review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for submitting R packages to rOpenSci's open software peer review and for volunteering to review; covers expectations, mandatory conduct, resources, and available templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our code of conduct is mandatory for everyone involved in our review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants in the review process (authors, reviewers, editors) must follow the rOpenSci code of conduct; see linked code of conduct for behavioral expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review to ensure consistent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: All the packages contributed by community members go through a process of open peer review to ensure a consistent level of quality for our users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review process is open (transparent) and intended to maintain consistent quality across packages submitted to rOpenSci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and purpose of review: non-adversarial and improvement-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim for our review process to be open, non-adversarial, and focused on improving software quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be constructive, framed as a two-way conversation, and oriented toward useful feedback and improving the package rather than adversarial criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value feedback (reason to submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should submit because they value the feedback; rOpenSci aims to provide useful feedback to package authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be open to and expect substantive feedback aimed at improving development practices and software quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet rOpenSci guidelines before/while submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages must meet rOpenSci guidelines; the review process also provides opportunity for discussion where exceptions are requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the ‘guide for authors’ and rOpenSci policies and aim to comply with the stated guidelines; if exceptions are needed these can be discussed during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the guide for authors before opening a submission issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to submit a package, read our guide for authors before opening a submission issue in this repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a procedural requirement: follow the instructions in the guide for authors to prepare and make a proper review request (see review_request_template).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers should read the guide for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: To volunteer as a reviewer, and to perform reviews, please read our guide for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing_guide.md contains expectations, recommended practices, and specifics on how to conduct reviews for rOpenSci; reviewers are expected to follow it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer reviewer onboarding (expertise & contact info)
rubrics_metrics.description: To volunteer to be one of our reviewers, please fill out this short form providing your contact information and areas or expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should register their areas of expertise and contact details so editors can match reviewers to submissions; rOpenSci seeks reviewers with general package-writing experience and domain expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the provided templates for submissions and reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Different templates are provided: review template, editor’s template, review request template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should use the relevant templates (e.g., review template for conducting reviews, review request template when submitting) to standardize submissions and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging and maintenance best practices (follow packaging guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: The gitbook includes chapters dedicated to good practice for package maintenance and a packaging_guide.md file is present in the repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the packaging guide and maintenance best practices (e.g., testing, documentation, dependency management) as described in the packaging_guide.md and maintenance chapters to meet expectations for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation website deployment (expected benefit/feature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Packages in our suite get a documentation website that is automatically built and deployed after each push.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their package is configured so documentation can be automatically built and deployed (CI/documentation site expectations) as part of being in the rOpenSci suite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-listing and downstream publication options
rubrics_metrics.description: rOpenSci packages can be cross-listed with other repositories such as CRAN and BioConductor; packages that contain a short accompanying paper can, after review, be automatically submitted to the Journal of Open-Source Software for fast-tracked publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are downstream benefits/paths available after successful review; authors who want cross-listing or JOSS submission should prepare appropriate artifacts (e.g., paper) and follow those processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing support and maintenance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once aboard, your package will continue to receive support from rOpenSci members. You’ll retain ownership and control of your package, but we can help with ongoing maintenance issues such as those associated with updates to R and dependencies and CRAN policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that rOpenSci provides ongoing support for maintenance-related issues; maintainers are expected to collaborate on upkeep but retain ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process is iterative and open to feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Our review process is always in development, and we encourage feedback and discussion on how to improve the process on our forum and in the ropensci/software-review-meta issue tracker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are encouraged to propose process improvements and discuss meta-level changes publicly (forum and meta issue tracker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial structure and transparent management
rubrics_metrics.description: The Software Peer Review process is run by a team of editors and an Editor-in-Chief (rotated), and the current status is visible on an interactive dashboard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should expect editorial oversight, reviewer assignment, and transparent tracking of submissions via the dashboard; editorial roles and responsibilities are defined in editors_guide.md.
